item.title: $4.7M state loan to go to housing complex at former Adobe Mexican Kitchen spot
item.description: The state on Tuesday approved a $4.7 million loan for a housing complex planned in Grand Rapids.

item.title: Local company planning tunnel to transport data center HVAC pipes between plants
item.description: A Michigan company plans on building a new tunnel to connect two facilities in Cascade Township.

item.title: Construction on I-96 in Ionia County will begin early
item.description: Construction will begin earlier than expected on I-96 this spring.

item.title: 'Surreal': Fremont student qualifies for Scripps National Spelling Bee
item.description: After years of hard work, a Fremont Middle School student will head to Washington in May to compete in the Scripps National Spelling Bee.

item.title: NTSB chair: LaGuardia crash investigator was stuck in TSA line for hours
item.description: The head of the National Transportation Safety Board said Monday that long lines at airport security checkpoints caused by the ongoing Department of Homeland Security (DHS) shutdown delayed investigators arriving at the scene of a deadly collision between a jet and a fire truck at LaGuardia International Airport.

item.title: Thunderstorms rumble across Southwest Michigan
item.description: A line of severe thunderstorms swept across Southwest Michigan Thursday evening.

item.title: 'Detrimental impact': GRPS superintendent moves to oust administrator
item.description: Grand Rapids Public Schools' superintendent is seeking to part ways with the district's deputy superintendent of preschool-12 learning and leadership, Brandy Lovelady Mitchell, over "concerns regarding her leadership and management style."

item.title: Prosecutor rules GRPD officer justified in deadly shooting
item.description: A Grand Rapids police officer was justified in his use of force when he shot and killed Da'Quain Johnson in February, the Kent County prosecutor ruled, deciding he would not file criminal charges in the case.

item.title: Western Michigan hockey will host outdoor game against University of Michigan in 2027
item.description: For the first time in school history, Western Michigan University hockey will host a game at Waldo Stadium in 2027.

item.title: Former Coldwater teacher accused of using technology to make child pornography
item.description: A former teacher already accused of setting up hidden cameras to spy on people in his own home is now accused of using technology to create child pornography.

item.title: GR leaders acknowledge pain, grief after no charges in deadly police shooting
item.description: Grand Rapids city leaders released statements after Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker announced he would not be charging the officers who shot and killed Da’Quain Johnson in February.

item.title: Family says fight continues after GRPD shooting ruled justified
item.description: Family and friends of Da’Quain Johnson gathered in the lobby of the Michigan State Police headquarters as, a few rooms away, Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker announced he would not be charging the officers who shot and killed him in February.

item.title: Longtime Ottawa County post office set to close at the end of the month
item.description: A longtime post office in Ottawa County is set to close at the end of April after losing its lease, forcing some residents to travel farther for everyday mail services.

item.title: Hegseth asks the Army's top uniformed officer to step down while US wages war against Iran
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has asked the Army’s top uniformed officer to step down, the Pentagon said Thursday without giving a reason for the departure as the United States wages a war against Iran.

item.title: Hope Network Center for Autism offers therapy, diagnoses
item.description: It’s World Autism Awareness Day. One West Michigan group is working to support families and help them find the resources they need.
